as...@hotmail.com wrote:
> I think imbued was a too drastical change to the VtES game (In fact,
> it´s more a totally new game!)

No, it's not. It would be a totally new game if the new set had
contained rules for, say, Shadowfist: the Eternal Ass-Whuppin'.

> Too many new rules at once.

People keep saying this, but I'm having a hard time seeing how there's
more of a learning curve for this set than any other set that doesn't
contain reprints.

Keep in mind that while NoR had more rules than most of the other sets,
it had *many* fewer cards. If you consider the total amount of learning
involved in remember both new rules and the effects of cards, I don't
think NoR is any higher on the curve than most other sets. Hell, people
still have questions about how Mata Hari's ability works.

> Too many cards/effects in play at once (5-6 cards on each imbued minion
> are not uncommon).

This has been another common complaint, but in a way it's a bit silly.
Once you've figured out what a given imbued can and can't do, you can
mostly stop worrying about any surprises coming from him, since most of
his cards are in play already. This is actually quite an advantage to
opponents of the imbued; while it seems like a pain in the ass now, I
think time will show that it's actually more detrimental to the imbued
player than anyone else.

> The symbols of the imbued "clans" is very hard to distinguish from
> eachother.

I agree. This is the one thing about the set that I felt could have
been handled better. White symbols on a black background (as someone
else here had suggested) would have been much more legible.

> Tempts to play the Gehenna events that locks down all constructive play
> from vampire decks.

That's a choice which is up to players. There's nothing that forces
anyone to play Gehenna events with the imbued.

> As a whole: Uncalled for, unbalanced and generally annoying.
>
> Poll: Was imbued a necessary addition to the game?

Not a necessary one, no. No set is a necessary addition to the game
(there is, in fact, no such thing as a necessary addition to the game).
But it's a set I'm glad was produced.

John Eno

Definitely not a new game. It doesn't really make sense to think of it
as one. Nearly every card in NoR requires or enables interaction
between the imbued and vampires.

> Too many new rules at once.

There are 5 "pages" of rules, one of which is merely a list of terms
and icons. They aren't too hard to learn. I recognize that even people
who don't want to learn them have to in order to make sure their
buddies are playing by the rules, but they aren't that complicated and
the person(s) who play the imbued can be responsible for bringing the
rules cards to the table so that everyone can double-check him.

> Too many cards/effects in play at once (5-6 cards on each imbued minion
> are not uncommon).

Only if no one plays intercept in your area.
In all seriousness they aren't any *more* problematic than the Una or
Mata Hari Freak Drive decks except that the cards are easier to get.

> The symbols of the imbued "clans" is very hard to distinguish from
> eachother.

Not to me, though I suppose I'm not the typical V:tES player.

> Tempts to play the Gehenna events that locks down all constructive play
> from vampire decks.

In my experience, these don't work terribly well, primarily because
they slow down the rest of your deck and generate more table-hate than
the imbued can handle. A moderate number of events that support a
particular strategy may be workable. Still if this is too much of a
problem, you can include anti-event or anti-ally tech in your deck and
deal with the problem directly - it's not like the cards you need
haven't been printed.

> As a whole: Uncalled for, unbalanced and generally annoying.

I totally disagree on all three points. There was at least as much call
to print the imbued as there was to print Gehenna events and all the
werewolf allies from KMW, or, for that matter, any card that doesn't
require a vampire to play. The imbued are quite well balanced, and if
you think they're too powerful, try Break the Code and intercept
combat. Annoying is a matter of taste, and well, it should be obvious
that my tastes run the other way.

> Poll: Was imbued a necessary addition to the game?

Only Jyhad was necessary for the game.
How useful was this poll question?

as...@hotmail.com wrote:
> I think imbued was a too drastical change to the VtES game (In fact,
> it´s more a totally new game!)

Not a new game as long as you can play your old deck.

> Too many new rules at once.

Too many? One new type of minion (imbued), and not entirely new, as
they are allies, two new types of cards (Powers and Convictions) with
their rules. Nothing to complain about, IMHO.

> Too many cards/effects in play at once (5-6 cards on each imbued minion
> are not uncommon).

This is true, I must admit it. But there already were deck with a lot
of cards on their minions - Raven Spies and Blood Dolls, for instance.

> The symbols of the imbued "clans" is very hard to distinguish from
> eachother.

Just take some time to learn them. Defenders, Judges Avengers and
Innocent are easy to recognize. Martyrs, Redeemers and Visionaries
symbols are more difficult to remember, but there isn't anything
impossible.

> Tempts to play the Gehenna events that locks down all constructive play
> from vampire decks.

There are NO cards that "locks down all constructive play from vampire
decks". Your statement is almost the same as if you said "Smiling Jack
eats the entire table". Somebody suffers more from the Gehenna events,
somebody less. Good Gehenna decks should make alliance with another
player.

> As a whole: Uncalled for, unbalanced and generally annoying.

As a whole: take your time to learn the new cards :) This set is too
distant from the traditional cards, I admit, and if you don't plan to
play Imbued, you won't find any usable cards in it (there are few
exceptions, like Break the Code, but...) That doesn't mean that it is
"annoying" or "unbalanced".

> Poll: Was imbued a necessary addition to the game?

Poll: Was Laibon a necessary addition to the game? Was Bloodlines a

necessary addition to the game?

Such "polls" are just stupid. The game really needs new mechanics, new
types of cards, and so on. They make the game more interesting AND help
to avoid the "critical mass" problem (the overall quality of existing
cards is constantly growing, and without adding new possibilities this
is going to FORCE players to buy new cards to remain competitive).
Please take a time to learn NoR and you will like it yourself.

Yours,
Ector

Messages.Author: Fred Scott

As is usually the case with things advertised as a "poll",
it isn't a poll, it's a thinly disguised stab at inciting
outrage. In the future, I want you guys to tag your posts
more correctly; e.g.:

Thinly Disguised Plea For Followers: Imbued Necessary?

<as...@hotmail.com> wrote in message
news:1149891259.9...@j55g2000cwa.googlegroups.com...

> I think imbued was a too drastical change to the VtES game (In fact,

> it愀 more a totally new game!)

> Too many new rules at once.

Frankly, I don't think it's matters how many new rules need to be
digested by players well-aquainted with the game at one time. The
long-term problem is how many _total_ rules need to be learned by
newcomers in order to play the game at all. We already know the
complexity of the game is a significant barrier to entry. We know
that to expand the game and add more depth to it (a good quality),
we have to pay the price in terms of additional rules (higher
complexity, harder to teach: a bad quality). So the real question
is, does the advantage of what the game gained outweigh the downside?

In this case, I would say not, as it turns out. I suppose I can't
blame anyone for trying, though. After all, you don't know how
something's going to turn out until you actually design the thing,
playtest and try to tune it, and then release it. By the time you
know whether it's good or bad, on balance, it's probably too late to
back up and call it off. (And it's not _that_ bad, really, IMHO.)

In retrospect, I do fault White Wolf for not putting more time and
dedicating a larger expansion to such a radical expansion. I think
it probably would have had a better shot if it hadn't been a mini-
expansion. That's sort of hindsight, though.

(other stuff ellided, either repititious or sort of quibbling, IMO)

> Poll: Was imbued a necessary addition to the game?

My reaction to this question is much the same as a lot of other
folks: no expansions are ever necessary. So that seems beside the
point.

Fred
